Lucas Henriksson

I am a third-year PhD student at the Stockholm School of Economics. I am also an affiliated researcher at the Research Group for Socioeconomic Studies of Technology at Lund University.
My research interests lie in the intersection of labor and public economics, with a particular focus on social security systems, unemployment and unions. I have also done policy work on taxation, with a focus on local and regional governments.

Union and Insurance Company? How Union-provided Unemployment Insurance affects Unionization Decisions
Studies how unions’ self-funded provision of unemployment insurance affects the recruitment of members. Specifically, I am investigating whether this explains the large and increasing gap in unionization rates between blue-collar and white-collar workers in Sweden.





Coauthored with Åsa Hansson. [Published by Ratio in 2025]
Summary in English: We analyzes the long-term sustainability of Sweden’s decentralized welfare model under growing fiscal pressure from demographic change, digitalization, and increased labor mobility. We examine the capacity of municipalities and regions to finance welfare services under a tax system dominated by local taxation of labor income. The report identifies structural weaknesses in the current financing model, including a shrinking and uneven local tax base, vertical tax externalities due to overlapping tax powers, and rising mobility of high-income earners. We discuss reforms to improve efficiency and long-term fiscal stability of the financing of local governments.



Coauthored with Åsa Hansson. [Published in KEFU 2026:3]
Summary in English: We analyze how Skåne’s future public welfare can be financed under increasing demographic pressure, mobility, and tax-base challenges. The report discusses alternative tax bases and systems that could increase the set of tools avaiable to local governments to finance welfare services.
